newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures soar to huge daily gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures soar to huge daily gains.

text.p: A buying spree by funds and dealers hoisted U.S. stock index futures to sharply higher and uncharted levels Thursday for a fifth consecutive day.
Lead-month September Standard & Poor's 500 futures vaulted 17.00 points higher to a new record-high of 896.40. They ended up 15.70 points at a new all-time high settlement of 895.10.

Brokers and analysts appeared somewhat surprised by the vigor and momentum of the rally, and they ticked off a litany of fundamental, technical and psychological factors as fueling Thursday's bull run, which occurred on heavy futures and cash turnover.

They pointed to a jump in U.S. Treasury bond futures prices after a weaker than expected May U.S. retail sales report stoked perceptions that U.S. demand is flagging and might discourage the Federal Reserve from hiking interest rates at its early-July meeting.
They also figured that soft consumer demand might trickle up to the wholesale level. Friday's May producer price index is forecast firming 0.1 percent overall and in the core rate.
Last week's breakout, a resilient broader market despite downside lapses in over-the-counter stocks, plus the closeness to psychologically key levels, added support, brokers said.
But brokers admitted they had trouble pinpointing any single compelling reason for the S&P rally other than the snowballing momentum as buyers scrambled to not miss the move.
"What could be here is an S&P market that has apparently a little longer legs as compared to the Nasdaq," said Jay Hohmann, head futures trader, Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
He also said cash S&P 500s' recent spike up made him wonder whether it is in the throes of a blow-off type rally.
"This is a big 'if' or a 'could be,'" he cautioned. "You must be careful of thinking that this thing can't extend itself for a while."
"I'm not really sure what's fueling the damned thing," admitted a busy floor broker in the final hour. "Even some of my traders haven't any idea why."
"The Dow's out of control, but it's not panicked (futures) buying," he added. "There's huge fund buying.... I think personally it's new (fund) buying."
Traders said buying revived late following a quick but brief setback after U.S. Treasury bond futures closed.
"We rallied to the highs at the bond close and then had a quick two-point setback," said another floor broker. "Then we had MOC (market-on-close) buying...it looked like arb buying."
Price boards estimated volume in the September and June S&P 500s at about 125,000 contracts combined, with brokers attributing roughly 20,000 of that solely to rollover.

September S&P 500s rallied 15.70 points to 895.10, Value Lines rose 8.25 to 781.20, Nikkei rose 295.0 to 20,700,0, Midcap rose 3.30 to 287.20, NYSE Composite rose 8.00 to 462.35, Russell rose 2.55 to 392.10, and Nasdaq rose 2.25 to 953.00.
